findings.passage: No one who was asked the million dollar question could muster the courage to answer what must be a 90% issue among the American electorate, neither for themselves or on behalf of their employers.  This sort of thing makes me want to look into just how many votes by our “guests” are disenfranchising lawfully cast American votes.
findings.note: Newsletter post about a 2026-01-29 committee hearing where lobbyists were asked whether only citizens should vote in Arizona elections. She comments on non-citizen voting.

findings.passage: In the Federalism, Military Affairs and Elections Committee, also on Wednesday, Representative Alex Kolodin’s HCR2001 was presented.  This is the “Florida Style” vote counting bill, which will also tighten up security on mail-in balloting (by mandating voters to verify addresses and request a mail-in ballot before each election), a measure that voters are begging for so our state isn’t the butt of all elections jokes.
findings.note: Newsletter describing HCR2001 in committee, including a requirement that voters verify address and request a mail ballot before each election.

findings.passage: Moving back to manageable precinct sizes will not only make elections smoother and reduce reliance upon mail-in balloting; it will help return voting to what it was supposed to be – a tradition of engaged citizenship rather than a passive, weeks-long game of ballot collection.
findings.note: Her speech excerpt on HCR 2016 (her own bill, small precincts) and mail voting. Related to election integrity; not about ID or citizenship proof.
